about: The one join between the two production flows (shared/PRODUCTION_FLOWS.md): whether a Sales Order line's production diverts to company stock when the order is cancelled after the goods were made. Both apps read this file in their tests.

fields.note: docstatus 2 is Frappe's own submit-cancel, separate from custom_sales_status. A line only needs diverting when it was being made for THIS order (mode = 'New Production'), not served from the shelf or claimed off a replenishment run - those belong to a pool already and cancelling the order just releases the claim.

needs_diversion.why: the plain case: the order was cancelled after the line had genuinely started production
an order that is merely rejected before approval, or otherwise still live, is not diverted - only an actual cancel (docstatus 2) triggers this
a draft order was never approved, so nothing was ever produced against it
a line served from the shelf belongs to the minimum-stock pool already - cancelling the order releases the reservation, it does not create a second batch
a line claimed off a replenishment run in progress is the run's stock, not this order's - it stays claimable by the next order rather than being diverted twice
a to-order line cancelled before production ever touched it was never made - diverting it would put a batch of goods nobody produced onto the shelf
Frappe's three spellings of an unset Data field are all the same 'never started', matching the rule stage_watch.json already pins
any non-empty stage means work began, whatever it currently reads - this is not asking how far production got, only whether it started

already_diverted.why: diverting is a one-time act - a production order already raised for this order/item pair must not be raised twice
a replenishment order (purpose stock) for the same item is a different pool and does not count as this order having been diverted
a diversion recorded against a different order does not cover this one, even for the same item
no orders at all is simply not diverted yet
